transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Recording: auto

Summary:
Redwood introduced hosting options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with emphasis on Dedicated + VPC for DocuTrace's regulatory needs. Core discussion focused on embedding dimensionality tradeoffs (128/512/1536), hybrid search (ANN + lexical), where to run rerank, and integration with their existing Milvus/FAISS-based vector store. Customer is evaluating cost vs latency, asks about tail latency guarantees and KV cache behavior when using long context and stateful reranking. Next steps: pricing, security docs, and an ops-focused benchmark.

Topics covered: deployment modes, embedding dims and quantization, batching and continuous KV cache, model fallbacks, vector DB connectors, sharding and replication strategies, pilot scope + success criteria.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Samir with Redwood, i'm the AE on this deal, will hand off to Maya for technical pieces, but first quick round robin?
[00:12] Ravi Menon: hi this is Ravi, lead search at DocuTrace, our main thing is search relevancy across millions of documents, latency targets under 200ms tail ideally, cost visibility is huge for us.
[00:23] Elena Gomez: Elena here, SRE, most concerned about VPC options, audit logs, kms, and how the inference nodes attach to our network.
[00:28] Tom Baker: Tom, CTO — want to understand if Redwood Dedicated actually reduces tail vs our current self-hosted p95 issues.
[00:35] Maya Chen: cool thanks, i'll share an overview of how we think about embedding + rerank pipelines, and then we'll map to DocuTrace's numbers. quick high level: two-stage retrieval -> embed ANN -> rerank using smaller cross-encoder or in-model rerank depending on latency.
[01:05] Maya Chen: so for the embedding dims you mentioned, Ravi, you said currently you experiment with 512 dims?
[01:09] Ravi Menon: yeah we started 512 but did a recent eval showing 1536 with bert-ish models gave better relevance for long documents; downside was throughput drop.
[01:18] Maya Chen: right that tracks; options are (1) keep 1536 but use quantization (8-bit / q4_0-ish) and dedicated GPUs to preserve throughput, or (2) reduce to 512 and run more QPS cheaply. there's also hybrid routing — use short-query 512 route for interactive search and fallback to 1536 for long-form or high-precision rerank.
[01:38] Elena Gomez: when you say quantization, do we lose recall? our legal team will ask about regression risk.
[01:44] Maya Chen: small regressions possible, we recommend eval sets and automatic quality monitoring. Redwood Optimize can give targeted quantization recommendations based on your evals; we also support rollbacks and A/B.
[02:05] Tom Baker: curious about the vector DB connectors — we have Milvus in prod but also a bunch of offline FAISS indices. how tight is that integration? do you host the vector store or do we keep ours?
[02:18] Samir Patel: good q. you can keep your DB, we provide connectors + SDKs for streaming inserts and lookups. with Dedicated you can colocate caching layers and RD request routing to reduce network hop. some customers choose Redwood-hosted vectors for simplicity, others keep their own for data residency.
[02:35] Ravi Menon: any thought on sharding? our doc corpus is ~120M vectors, need sharding + cross-shard fanout.
[02:43] Maya Chen: for ~100M range we recommend sharding by logical partition (customer id / namespace) and use routing policies to reduce cross-shard queries. Redwood's routing can do top-k fanout optimization — call fewer shards initially and expand if needed. note that fanout increases tail latency and cost.
[03:10] Elena Gomez: how about KV cache — we rely on prefix caching for multi-turns, do you support long-lived kv state?
[03:18] Maya Chen: yes continuous KV cache with LRU and explicit pinning. slight note: with Dedicated we give stronger guarantees around cache locality; in Private you self-manage. sometimes the transcript generator mis-heard it as K-V cash earlier in other calls, sorry for that.
[03:38] Ravi Menon: we want to run rerank as a secondary step with a cross-encoder for top-100 results; cost estimate?
[03:46] Maya Chen: typical approach: embed dense retriever to get top-1k or 100, then rerank top-100 with cross-encoder. On Dedicated with batching and GPU-optimized kernels you can get ~5-10ms per item at scale depending on model. cost depends on batch efficiency and whether you run in GPU pool. we can model it in the pilot.
[04:20] Tom Baker: what's an example pilot? we prefer a 2-week scoped benchmark with 3 workloads: low-latency queries (99th <200ms), high-recall batch rerank, and indexing throughput.
[04:30] Samir Patel: that's exactly what we typically do: 2 weeks, ingest pipe + 50k queries / sec sim, run p50/p95/p99 and compare. we'll include a dedicated infra config and fallback policies.
[04:50] Priya Shah: small question on security: if we go Dedicated in our VPC, does Redwood touch plaintext? we need to know about KMS keys.
[04:58] Maya Chen: with Private you control KMS and keys, with Dedicated we can support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) via KMS/HSM integrations, and we can limit that plaintext never leaves your VPC. we'll send the architecture doc.
[05:20] Ravi Menon: competitor check — Pinecone's pricing is getting us worried, they advertise lower TCO but their tail latency was worse in our last eval.
[05:30] Samir Patel: yep we've seen that. Pinecone/Weaviate offer good managed vector dbs but Redwood differentiates by combining inference runtime with routing and caching so you can optimize end-to-end.
[05:45] Elena Gomez: do you have SLA for tail latency on Dedicated?
[05:49] Maya Chen: we offer latency SLO guidance and can include SLOs in Dedicated contracts; exact p99 guarantee depends on committed capacity and model choice.
[06:05] Ravi Menon: ok let's talk numbers — we expect peak 6k qps for search queries with an average doc length of 1.2k tokens, and rerank at ~400 qps.
[06:16] Maya Chen: for those numbers, Dedicated with autoscaling bursts makes sense; we can size GPU pools to handle 6k embedding qps (1536 dims with quantization) plus rerank pool for cross-encoder. batching improves throughput but increases latency — continuous batching helps flatten that.
[06:40] Tom Baker: any plan to reduce cost via model routing? like cheaper embedding model for recall first pass then heavier model for final?
[06:48] Maya Chen: yes hybrid routing is recommended — run a fast 512-d embedding model for initial recall then route selected candidates to a high-dim 1536 or a cross-encoder rerank. Redwood's routing policies let you configure thresholds and fallbacks.
[07:05] Priya Shah: alerting / observability — we need token-level cost, per-route latency breakdown and tracing into the vector DB.
[07:14] Maya Chen: Redwood Console gives per-route dashboards, token/cost breakdowns and tracing hooks; we can also push traces to your observability stack.
[07:30] Ravi Menon: can you talk about quantization toolchain — are you using post-training quantization or QAT?
[07:37] Maya Chen: mostly post-training quantization for embeddings, plus some customers run light QAT; we recommend running a regression check in Redwood Optimize before enabling globally.
[08:05] Tom Baker: question on network egress — if we keep Milvus, how many network hops are typical if Dedicated is in our VPC?
[08:15] Samir Patel: minimal — with VPC peering/private endpoints you get single hop to your vector db; with hosted vector store it can be multi-hop. we'll document recommended network setup.
[08:40] Elena Gomez: we also need SOC 2 + compliance artifact review and penetration test logs.
[08:46] Samir Patel: will send SOC 2 and compliance pack; we can also set up an NDA channel for pen test artefacts.
[09:00] Maya Chen: wanted to flag a small gotcha: when using high-dim embeddings + heavy rerank, KV cache becomes larger and GPU memory matters — you might need multi-GPU or model sharding.
[09:18] Ravi Menon: is model sharding supported? we have some long sequence reranks.
[09:23] Maya Chen: yes, runtime supports model parallelism and kernel selection for long sequence. if you go Private we can work on on-prem packaging too.
[09:40] Tom Baker: ok sounds good. last thing — do you provide turnkey vector DB migration tools?
[09:47] Maya Chen: we have connectors and streaming ingest helpers; for large corpuses we help with bulk migration scripts and parallel loaders.
[10:05] Samir Patel: quick recap: DocuTrace wants a 2-week pilot to validate tail latency for 6k qps search + 400 qps rerank, evaluate 1536 vs 512 dims with quantization, and verify VPC/KMS controls. Redwood will send pricing, SOC2 + KMS docs and run an ops benchmark lead by Maya.
[10:30] Ravi Menon: agreed, and we'll share sample dataset and our Milvus sharding config.
[10:40] Elena Gomez: i'll coordinate infra access and network setup for the benchmark.
[10:50] Tom Baker: put together a pilot SOW and timeline and we'll get procurement involved.
[11:00] Samir Patel: awesome, i'll follow up with an email and attach the SOW template. thanks all.
